items.caption:
When did you last clean yours? 

Extractor hood filters hold onto grease, grime and some pretty awful cooking smells 🤢 so they definitely need a good clean every so often!

And before anyone says “just put them in the dishwasher!” 😂 Not all filters are dishwasher-safe, and the dishwasher can tarnish some finishes.

I prefer cleaning mine like this with bicarb, or giving them a good soak in warm soapy water with a little white vinegar.

But come on… cleaning them like this is FAR more satisfying to watch! 😍✨

Be honest… when did you last clean yours? 

#queenofclean #amsr #satisfyingcleaning

QUEEN OF CLEAN’S BACK-TO-SCHOOL STAIN-BUSTING KIT ✨🎒

Don’t just get the school uniform ready… get your stain-busting kit ready too! 🙌

I’ve put together some of my favourite essentials to keep under the sink, ready to tackle those inevitable school stains. 🧼

From keeping white polo shirts looking pristine 🤍 to stopping black trousers from looking dull and faded 🖤 these simple tips will help keep that uniform looking fresher for longer.

Now tell me… 👇

Which tip is your favourite? And which one did you NOT already know? 👀

#backtoschool #stainremovers #laundryhacks
items.transcript: I'm always asked about kids' stains. So I thought what I would do today is, back to school is starting to loom up, parents are starting to think about school uniform, bits and pieces. Why don't we put together a queen of clean, back to school stain busting kit. Let's go and do it. Best product I would add would be good old bicarbonate of soda because it's great for brightening white socks and great for deodorising PE kits. White vinegar is another favourite, pretty much the same as the bicarb here. It's going to help deodorise those sports kits. So I would always, when their PE kit comes in, that's been in their bag for a week and a bit smelly, put some white vinegar in some warm water and let it soak for a few hours before washing. Nylon in black. So I remember when my kids were at school, you'd buy a black pair of trousers and like halfway through the year you'd put them next to another pair of black trousers and you can see that the black has started to fade. So this is going to keep them looking pristine and brand new without you buying new pairs. You know how much I love a sieve cream cleaner. So this is definitely one for that back to school kit. This is really good at keeping the soles of white trainers looking pristine and box fresh. Colour catchers. These are always good because sometimes you get polo shirts and you've got a blue logo on a white polo shirt. Colour can run. So the first few washes, I'd always recommend using a colour catcher. If you've got young girls that wear school tights, I never forget like how tangled the washing used to come out and you'd spend like half an hour trying to detangle them. So you're going to want to get yourself some laundry mesh bags in that kit for the school tights. Magic erasers. You wouldn't believe it, but you know like your school bag, your lunchbox, sometimes you get marks on even the pencil case. Damp on one of these, just take those marks off. It saves you putting it through the wash. Also good on your trainers as well.

#teatowels #queenofclean #cleaningtips
items.transcript: Today's question I've had in is my tea towels, they smell clean but they've got a bit of a musty odour. Now most people, let's be honest and hold our hands up, even I can do this, are a tea towel abuser. So your poor little tea towel doesn't just dry dishes, it does so much more. So how do we keep it clean? When it comes to tea towels, you know what, I love a good old school like terry towel tea towel. They're so much better at soaking up those soapy suds. So if your tea towel's got any stains on it, I would grab some white vinegar and just liberally spray all of those stains like ketchup stains, food stains. Tea towels are just quite stainy, aren't they? So liberally spray with white vinegar, leave it for 15 minutes before washing. We're going to ditch the fabric conditioner because that takes away the absorbency. And for keeping it nice and white and bright, if you've got white tea towels, you're going to add in a nice big scoop of bicarbonate of soda. So they've actually run out in here, which is a real shame, but I would then add a laundry cleanser to the wash. It's just going to give them that extra boost, kill that bacteria and keep your tea towels looking as good as new.
